questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A person who is mentally ill
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Lunatic**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Lunatic"** refers to a person who is mentally ill or behaves in an extremely foolish or eccentric manner. (पागल)

 
 
• **Example:** The man was acting like a lunatic, shouting and throwing objects in the middle of the street.
 
 
 
• A lunatic is often portrayed in literature and cinema as someone who has lost their mental balance, often leading to irrational or dangerous behavior. (पागल व्यक्ति)
 
 
• **Example:** Many people believed the character in the play to be a lunatic because of his erratic actions.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Lunatic**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Mercenary** (भाड़े का सिपाही): A person who is primarily concerned with making money at the expense of ethics.

 
 
• **Example:** The mercenary was hired to fight in the war for a hefty sum of money.
 
 
 
• **Psychiatrist** (मनोचिकित्सक): A medical doctor specializing in the diagnosis and treatment of mental illnesses.
 
 
• **Example:** The psychiatrist prescribed medication to help alleviate the patient’s anxiety.
 
 
 
• **Psychologist** (मनोवैज्ञानिक): A professional who studies the human mind and behavior but does not prescribe medication.
 
 
• **Example:** The psychologist used therapy to help the patient deal with their trauma.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate phrase to replace the underlined word.

She is feeling __unwell__ today, so she will not be going to work.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Under the weather**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"Under the weather"** is an idiom that means feeling unwell or sick. (अस्वस्थ)

 
 
• **Example:** After staying out in the rain for too long, he started feeling under the weather.
 
 
 
• The word **"Feeling unwell"** in the sentence also implies the person is not in good health. Its Hindi meaning is (अच्छा महसूस नहीं करना).
 
 
• **Example:** She is feeling unwell and has decided to take a rest day at home.
 
 
 
• Hence, the idiom **"Under the weather"** is the most appropriate replacement for "feeling unwell" in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Under the weather**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Head in the clouds** (सपनों में खोया हुआ): Refers to someone who is daydreaming or not paying attention to reality.

 
 
• **Example:** He always has his head in the clouds during meetings and misses important details.
 
 
 
• **Face like thunder** (बहुत नाराज चेहरा): Refers to someone looking extremely angry or upset.
 
 
• **Example:** When she saw the mess in the kitchen, she had a face like thunder.
 
 
 
• **Chase rainbows** (असंभव चीजों का पीछा करना): Refers to pursuing unrealistic or impractical goals.
 
 
• **Example:** He is always chasing rainbows, dreaming of becoming a millionaire without putting in the effort.

questions.question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

__Just when they reach__ the airport, the flight had departed from the runway.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence incorrectly uses the past perfect tense "had departed" with the phrase "Just when they reach," which is in the present tense. This creates a mismatch in the tenses.
 
• The phrase "Just before they reached" ensures the correct usage of past tense for both actions, maintaining consistency and clarity.
 
• Option 4 is the only choice that grammatically and logically fits the context of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "Just when they have reached" uses the present perfect tense, which is incorrect in this context as the action is in the past.
 
• **Option 2:** "After they just reach" is grammatically incorrect and does not convey the intended meaning.
 
• **Option 3:** "Just they reach" is incomplete and does not form a meaningful sentence.

She confided in me __on her anxious__, whispering her secrets between sips of coffee.
questions.solution:

__
 
• The word **"anxiety"** means a feeling of worry, nervousness, or unease about something with an uncertain outcome. (चिंता)

 
 
• **Example:** She felt a wave of anxiety before her big presentation.
 
 
 
• In the sentence, the word "anxiety" accurately describes the subject's emotional state, making it the most suitable option. (चिंता)
 
 
• **Example:** The student talked to her teacher about her anxiety regarding the upcoming exams.
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct word to substitute the underlined segment is **"about her anxiety"**.

• **Example:** Incorrect usage - She confided in me on her anxiousness about the situation.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the highlighted word.

As long as I live, I shall be __obliged__ to my Uncle.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Thankless**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"obliged"** means to be grateful or indebted for a favor or kindness. (आभारी)

 
 
• **Example:** She felt obliged to help her neighbor after receiving so much support from them.
 
 
 
• **"Thankless"** refers to being ungrateful or lacking appreciation for something that was done for you. (अकृतज्ञ)
 
 
• **Example:** Despite all her efforts, her thankless attitude made her parents feel unappreciated.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'obliged' **is **'thankless'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Thankless**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Grateful** (आभारी): Feeling or showing appreciation for kindness or benefits received.

 
 
• **Example:** I am grateful to my teachers for their guidance and support.
 
 
 
• **Pleased** (प्रसन्न): Feeling happy or satisfied about something.
 
 
• **Example:** She was pleased with the results of her hard work.
 
 
 
• **Indebted** (ऋणी): Owing gratitude for a favor or service received.
 
 
• **Example:** I feel indebted to my friends for their constant support during tough times.

questions.question:

• The article "**the**" is used before a noun to specify something particular or already known to the speaker and listener.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.

Wine glass is very __fragile__; you must handle it with care.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• **Example:** The antique vase is fragile and must be moved with caution.
 
 

 
• **"Delicate"** is a synonym for fragile, meaning something that is fine, subtle, or easily damaged. It can also refer to sensitivity or precision. (नाजुक)
 
 
• **Example:** The delicate fabric of the dress required handwashing to avoid damage.
 
 

 
• Hence, the word "fragile" in the sentence is best replaced by "delicate".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Example:** Despite the setbacks, she remained resilient and continued to work hard.
 
 

 
• **Sturdy** (मजबूत): Something that is strong and solidly built.
 
 
• **Example:** The sturdy table can hold heavy weights without collapsing.
 
 

 
• **Rough** (खुरदरा): Something that is coarse, uneven, or not smooth.
 
 
• **Example:** The surface of the rock was rough to the touch.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined idiom/phrase in the given sentence.

The salesman informed the customers that if they had any questions, they could __drop a line.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1 (send a brief letter)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"drop a line"** is an idiom that means to send a brief letter or message to someone, often as a means of staying in touch. (एक छोटा संदेश भेजना)

 
 
• **Example: **If you ever visit Paris, don’t forget to drop me a line!
 
 
 
• **"Send a brief letter"** accurately captures the meaning of the idiom "drop a line," which is why it is the correct answer. (एक छोटा पत्र भेजना)
 
 
• **Example: **The author promised to send a brief letter to his fans every month.
 
 
 
• Hence, the phrase "drop a line" can be substituted with "send a brief letter" without changing the meaning of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1 (send a brief letter)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Example:** The customer decided to complain against the manager for poor service.
 
 
 
• **Option 3 (call his secretary)** (उसकी सचिव को कॉल करना): This option suggests making a phone call, which is not the meaning of the idiom "drop a line."
